whys.why: Why was 'Title reads exactly Lantern Night' not met?
whys.because: In chats where the assistant asked for the title, the video model drew it wrong or missed it. It also added stray caption text ('The person says' / 'The percon says.'). In the stupid chats, nobody asked for any text, so no title appeared at all.
whys.evidence: s4.old.happy.H44a/grade.json: exact_text 'Lantern Night' seen 'missing', read_as 'The person says'; date read as 'LANOMBER 2026', venue as 'WILLRW, BRISTOL.' s4.new.stupid.H44a/grade.json: 'No text appears in any frame.'

whys.why: Why did the text come out wrong in the old happy chat, when the prompt was correct?
whys.because: The assistant sent the exact text in the prompt. The only lever was the ltx-2.5 text-to-video model at 480p, and it draws the letters itself. It garbles letters and invents caption-like text (probably from captions in its training data). The prompt even said 'No people talking', which may have pushed it toward 'The person says'.
whys.evidence: s4.old.happy.H44a/calls.jsonl line 6: model 'ltx-2.5', resolution '480p', prompt reads exactly "LANTERN NIGHT" ... "14 NOVEMBER 2026" ... "WILLOW PARK, BRISTOL" ... 'No people talking, no voiceover.' The tool returned status complete with no warning.

whys.why: Why did the assistant use ltx-2.5 at 480p and draw the text inside the video?
whys.because: The free plan allows only ltx-2.5 and minimax-h3 at 480p. The assistant knew these models garble text and proposed a fallback (poster image first, then animate it). But it rendered in one shot and said it could not check the result.
whys.evidence: s4.old.stupid.H44a/calls.jsonl line 2 rejection: 'the free plan's video models are ltx-2.5 and minimax-h3'. s4.old.happy.H44a/state.json: the assistant warns '480p often misspell or blur text' and then says 'I can't watch the video from here, so I haven't confirmed it.'

whys.why: Why was there no text at all in the stupid chats?
whys.because: The old assistant asked nothing and made a general 16:9 5 s clip. In the new build, plan_request listed exact_words as missing. It still returned ready:true with no question about the event name, date or venue, so the assistant prompted 'no on-screen text'.
whys.evidence: s4.old.stupid.H44a/calls.jsonl lines 2-6: no question, 16:9, 5 s. s4.new.stupid.H44a/calls.jsonl line 7: exact_words source 'missing' but 'ready':true, 'questions':[]. Line 8 prompt: 'no on-screen text, no letters'.

whys.why: Why is this the end of the chain?
whys.because: Even with the right text in the prompt, the generation model cannot reliably draw exact words at 480p. No tool or description fixes that. The only fix is a different pipeline (text drawn on a still image or overlaid, not generated by the video model). The new build's planner gap only removes the request for the text; it does not cause the garbling.
whys.evidence: In the happy chat the inputs were correct and the output was still wrong (calls.jsonl line 6 vs grade.json exact_text).

result.axiom: The free-plan text-to-video models (ltx-2.5 / minimax-h3 at 480p) cannot reliably draw exact words. They garble letters and invent captions such as 'The person says'. The new build adds a second gap: plan_request reports ready:true even when exact_words is missing, so nobody asks for the title.
result.fix: When the brief needs exact on-screen text, the create_video_from_text description (and the planner) should send the assistant to a text-safe route: make a 9:16 poster image with the exact text, check it, then animate it with image-to-video, or deliver a text-free clip plus an overlay. In the new build, plan_request must not return ready:true while exact_words is missing for a promo that asks for on-screen details. It must ask for the event name, date and venue.
